Basis for Intervening:
Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.214, Evergy Kansas Central, Inc.; Evergy Metro, Inc.; and Evergy Missouri West, Inc. (collectively “the Companies”), all subsidiaries of Evergy, Inc. (“Evergy”), respectfully move to jointly intervene in Docket No. RR27-1-000, relating to the North American Electric Reliability Corporation’s (“NERC”) petition for approval of revisions to the NERC Rules of Procedure regarding computational loads. In support of their Motion, the Companies state:

Evergy is a multistate electric utility holding company system providing electric service at retail and wholesale through the Companies.  The Companies provide electric service at retail throughout Kansas and Missouri to approximately 1.6 million customers and provide wholesale service to municipalities and cooperatives that in turn serve additional Kansas and Missouri retail customers.  The Companies are Transmission Owners in SPP and have placed their transmission facilities under the SPP Open Access Transmission Tariff.  Through their Generation and Marketing divisions, the Companies are active participants in the wholesale electric market.  The Companies are also major Transmission Customers in SPP, purchasing transmission service for their retail load, point-to-point service for their energy marketing activities, and acting as an agent for certain wholesale customers in purchasing transmission service on their behalf.  Moreover, the Companies are also Load Responsible Entities that are responsible for interconnecting large loads.  Evergy is a NERC Registered Entity, and is registered under multiple functions.

Based on Evergy’s status as a NERC Registered Entity, the Companies will be directly impacted by the outcome of this proceeding, and their interests cannot be represented by any other party. The Companies therefore respectfully request to intervene in the above-referenced proceeding.
